$comment: PE/COFF EXECUTABLE (PE32+) for x86_64 Windows. Second PE schema (plan 14 LK2 cycle 2, 2026-05-30). Consumed by `src/link/format/pe.cpp` via the format-blind linker engine. Differs from `pe64-x86_64-windows.format.json` (the .obj schema) in: `pe.type = exec`; sections carry `virtualAddress` (interpreted as RVA — offset from ImageBase); top-level `entryPoint` names the entry symbol (resolved against AssembledModule at link time); new `optionalHeader` block populated with IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64 fields. ImageBase = 0x140000000 (Windows x86_64 .exe convention per the MSVC linker default). Subsystem = IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_WINDOWS_CUI (3) — console subsystem; GUI exe would set 2. SectionAlignment = 0x1000 (4 KB page); FileAlignment = 0x200 (512 bytes, MSVC default).
$dataModelComment: FC3 c1: 64-bit Windows is LLP64 (int 32, long 32, long long 64, ptr 64). Consumed by the semantic tier (buildCuMir threads format.dataModel() into analyze()): c long binds I32 here, the literal ladder + descriptor signatureByDataModel resolve their LLP64 arms. REQUIRED closed-enum field; the loader rejects a missing or unknown value (a silent default would bake wrong widths).
$headerNameMatchingComment: D-PP-HEADER-CASE-INSENSITIVE-PE: Windows filesystems (NTFS, FAT) match file names case-INSENSITIVELY, and the Windows SDK depends on it -- sqlite3.c:67322 spells `#include <Windows.h>` with a capital W while the shipped descriptor is `windows.json`. REQUIRED closed-enum field. DSS ASCII-folds the comparison ITSELF per path component (core/types/include_path_resolve.cpp) instead of asking fs::exists, so this resolves identically whether the build host is NTFS or ext4 -- MEASURED before the axis existed: rc=0 through /mnt/c, rc=1 error[F001A] on ext4, SAME binary, SAME commit.
$cSymbolDecorationComment: D-FFI-CMANGLING-RULE-NOT-CONFIG-DRIVEN: PE/COFF x64 applies NO decoration to a C identifier. The leading-underscore cdecl convention belongs to 32-bit x86 PE, which DSS does not ship; the 32-bit `_func` and stdcall `_func@N` rules arrive as their own scheme enumerators WITH their engine arms, never as a re-spelling of this one. MEASURED 2026-08-06 (`objdump -p C:/Windows/System32/ucrtbase.dll`, GNU binutils via WSL): the UCRT exports `exit`, `_exit` AND `_Exit` as three DISTINCT entries -- so the underscored spelling is not a decoration of `exit` here either, it already names a different function, and a format that wrongly claimed `leading-underscore` would silently bind to it. Consistent with this family's own `processExit.importMangledName`, the undecorated `exit`. This key is the single owner of a fact that previously had TWO: the closed C++ table `kCManglingRules` (src/ffi/mangling/c_mangle.cpp, keyed on ObjectFormatKind) and, redundantly, a literal encoding in the descriptors themselves -- the macho64-*-exec files spell `processExit.importMangledName` as `_exit` while their elf/pe siblings spell it `exit`. Two owners in two languages, with nothing forcing them to agree. RED-ON-DISABLE, stated precisely for the tier that exists today (MEASURED 2026-08-06 by actually removing the key from a shipped file and running the suite): DELETE this key and the format is REFUSED AT LOAD -- TWO errors at /cSymbolDecoration, one C_MissingField from the loader and one from ObjectFormatData::validate(), which loadFromText runs before returning -- so every test and example that loads this format goes red, naming the file. CHANGING the value is now an equally REAL lever, and this sentence was corrected the moment it became true: before step C4 the engine still read a C++ table and the value here changed no emitted binary. C4 landed (same cycle, TF-C122), and the effect is MEASURED 2026-08-06 -- flipping macho64-arm64-darwin-exec from `leading-underscore` to `none` and RECOMPILING NOTHING made the engine emit `printf` where it had emitted `_printf`, reddening tests/ffi/test_c_mangle.cpp's SchemeIsReadFromTheShippedSchemaNotACppTable. That is the whole point of the anchor: the answer lives in this file, so editing this file changes what the compiler emits. Two further pins guard the value: tests/link/test_c_symbol_decoration.cpp asserts the per-kind answer across all 24 shipped files and cross-checks it against this family's own processExit.importMangledName.
$cCallingConventionComment: D-FFI-ABI-CATALOG-SELECTS-CALLING-CONVENTION-BY-FORMAT-IDENTITY: the platform C ABI for code compiled into this format, NAMING a row in the paired target's callingConventions[] array. Microsoft x64 (`rcx,rdx,r8,r9` + 32 bytes of shadow space) — the SAME x86_64 processor as the elf64/macho64 descriptors, a DIFFERENT convention, which is why the fact is per-FORMAT and cannot live on the target.
$outputExtensionComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the extension the driver appends to an artifact this format produces. This used to be derived in C++ by `program/target_spec.cpp::outputExtensionFor`, a five-arm `switch (fmt.kind())` with a NESTED per-flavor switch inside each arm -- seven identity mentions computing a NAMING fact, which is not an engine behaviour at all. The nest existed because one ObjectFormatKind spans several artifact flavors; a DOCUMENT is exactly one flavor, so the whole derivation collapses to this one string. REQUIRED on every format. An EMPTY value is a DECLARED answer and not an omission -- a Unix executable carries no extension -- which is why the in-memory field is an `optional` and the loader's required check asks `contains`, never `empty`.
$archiveFlavorComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: WHICH `ar` variant this format's ECOSYSTEM uses. Declared on every native format, not only the `container: archive` ones, because that is what the deleted C++ derivation answered: `(format.kind() == ObjectFormatKind::Pe) ? Coff : SysV` was handed WHATEVER format the caller had, and `linkAndWriteStaticArchive` is reachable with the RELOCATABLE format of an ecosystem as well as its archive one (MEASURED -- restricting the key to archives reddened link/test_ar_writer and program/test_static_link). NOT cosmetic: the coff flavor carries the little-endian second linker member link.exe requires to resolve members at all. A closed VERB rather than an open name, because an archive layout is an ENGINE capability -- only variants `writeArArchive` realizes can be honored.
$targetArchComment: D-PROGRAM-TIER-RETAINS-FORMAT-IDENTITY-BRANCHES: the .target.json NAME this format is for. `crossValidateTargetFormat` compares it against TargetSchema::name() -- two DECLARED NAMES -- where it used to run a six-arm `switch (format.kind())` reading a DIFFERENT field per identity (elf.machine / pe.machine / macho.cputype) and compare each against a hardcoded C++ table, kTargetArchMachineCodes, keyed on (target name x format kind). THAT TABLE IS DELETED, and the argument is ONE OWNER rather than tidiness: `arm64 is EM_AARCH64 = 183` had two owners -- this document's own machine field and that C++ row -- with nothing forcing them to agree, which is the identical shape as kCManglingRules and kAbiCatalog. The number now lives only in the document that emits it, and the pairing question is answered by a name this document states outright. Adding a new arch is now JSON-ONLY.
$predefinedMacrosComment: TF-C97 (D-PP-FORMAT-DATA-MODEL-PREDEFINES): THIS FORMAT DELIBERATELY DECLARES NO `predefinedMacros`, and the absence is an ANSWER rather than an omission -- it is the whole reason the channel lives on the FORMAT and not on the target. `dataModel` above is LLP64, so `__LP64__`/`_LP64` must NOT be defined here: MEASURED 2026-07-30, `/usr/bin/clang -dM -E -x c /dev/null -target x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` (Apple clang 21.0.0) defines NEITHER, while the SAME clang defines BOTH on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu and x86_64-apple-darwin -- the same CPU, differing only by object format, which is precisely why a target-side row would be a lie on this leg. Adding either spelling here would make the Windows headers take their LP64 arms against a 32-bit `long`. Pinned in the NEGATIVE direction by tests/link/test_object_format_schema.cpp.
$bitFieldStrategyComment: D-CSUBSET-BITFIELD-ABI-EXACT: C bit-field allocation is OS/format-determined (the x86_64 CPU target serves BOTH this PE format and ELF-SysV), so the strategy lives here, not on the target. MSVC's x64 ABI starts a NEW allocation unit — aligned to the field's declared-type natural alignment — whenever an adjacent bit-field's declared-type SIZE differs from the current unit's type size (it never packs different-sized declared types into one unit), and the struct size covers the last unit's full declared-type width. Byte-ABI-exact to cl.exe (verified by the conformance witness): e.g. `{int a:1; char b:1;}` is sizeof 8 with b@byte4, vs gnu_packed's 4 with b@bit1.
$longDoubleFormatComment: FC17.9(e) D-CSUBSET-LONG-DOUBLE: MSVC x64 `long double` IS `double` (64-bit IEEE, 8/8) — the f64 axis collapses the c `long double` row to F64, so the full double machinery serves it end-to-end (the LLP64 long==int identity-collapse precedent). OS/format-determined (the same x86_64 target serves ELF-SysV's x87-80), so the axis lives here next to dataModel.
$entryPointComment: Empty entryPoint defaults the walker to module.functions[0] (cycle-2 convention — same as LK1 ELF ET_EXEC). Real-name resolution closes with D-LK1-1 (HIR→LIR symbol-name thread). D-LK10-ENTRY Slice C (CLOSED 2026-06-02, commit 1a0b414): the linker prepends a synthetic `_start` trampoline as module.functions[0]; the schema's empty entryPoint resolves to functions[0] = the trampoline, which then calls the USER fn (the post-prepend functions[1+]). See plan 14 §2.13 — Stage 1 closed.
$externCallDispatchComment: PE resolves imports through IAT import THUNKS: the linker synthesizes one `jmp *[IAT slot]` code thunk per extern (the PE analog of an ELF PLT stub / Mach-O __stubs entry) and points each extern symbol's VA at its THUNK, so an extern reference — a direct call OR an address-taken value — is a callable code address. The call site is a plain direct `call rel32 -> thunk` (x86_64 E8 disp32); the thunk does the IAT indirection. `indirect-slot` (symbolVa = the raw .idata data slot) MISCOMPILES an address-taken import: `call *reg` through the slot executes data as code (sqlite os_win.c aSyscall[] — the pe64 leg's last run-green blocker). D-FFI-EXTERN-CALL-DISPATCH + D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK.
$dataImportBindingComment: c149 (D-LK-EXTERN-DATA-IMPORT, the PE half — the LAST missing image binding model): extern library DATA objects (msvcrt `_fmode` / `_environ`-class data exports) bind via the IAT SLOT ITSELF — PE `__imp_<name>` semantics: the loader import-resolves EVERY IAT slot to the exported symbol's ADDRESS (function or data alike), so for a data import the `.idata` slot IS a loader-filled pointer to the object. This is exactly the Mach-O `__got` non-lazy-pointer model — the SAME `got-indirect` enum value, no new vocabulary. The linker binds symbolVa[dataExtern] to the IAT slot VA (pe.cpp — FUNC externs → their `FF 25` .text THUNK VA per D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK, DATA externs → the `.idata` IAT slot VA; NO thunk is emitted for a data extern: a data object is not callable, and a data reference resolved to a thunk VA would read jump-stub BYTES as the object's value — the exact silent-miscompile class the linker's data-import gate guards). MIR→LIR materializes the object's address by lea-of-slot + deref (the shared GotIndirect lowering Mach-O uses — zero lowering changes). The ELF exec formats declare this SAME value now: their copy-relocation model was DELETED (D-LK-ELF-COPY-RELOC-CLAIMS-ONE-NAME-OF-AN-ALIAS-SET — it claimed one name of an aliased libc object and split it silently), so `got-indirect` is the only data-import model in the vocabulary and every image format shares it.
$processExitComment:
D-LK10-ENTRY Slice B (plan 14 §2.13): the Windows runnable-binary spine. Trampoline emitter issues a plain `call rel32` to the CRT `exit` THUNK (direct-plt, per D-FFI-PE-IMPORT-THUNK; was `call qword ptr [iat_...]` under the retired indirect-slot model). The linker injects a synthetic `ExternImport{ucrtbase.dll, exit}` into module.externImports; the IAT writer (LK6 cycle 2a) emits the IAT slot, the import-thunk synthesis emits a `jmp *[iat_exit]` code thunk in .text, and the universal `call` LIR opcode emits E8 disp32 with a REL32 reloc on the disp32 patch site targeting the synthetic import's SymbolId (resolved to the thunk VA).

★★ TF-C111 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION P3) REPOINTED THIS FROM kernel32 `ExitProcess` TO ucrtbase `exit`, AND THE ARGUMENT IT REPLACES IS RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN DELETED, because that argument was long, load-bearing, and is now FALSE IN EVERY CLAUSE. It read: 'ExitProcess ALREADY flushes the msvcrt stdio buffers... when ExitProcess runs, the loader sends DLL_PROCESS_DETACH to every loaded DLL in reverse-load order, and msvcrt.dll's detach handler flushes + closes its CRT streams... switching PE to call msvcrt `exit` would be a regression risk for ZERO benefit'. Every one of those sentences was ABOUT msvcrt, and the pe CRT is no longer msvcrt.

WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED, AND WHY IT IS NOT OPTIONAL: msvcrt's DLL-detach handler ran the application's `atexit` onexit table on its way out, so `ExitProcess` happened to deliver C's return-from-main semantics for free. UCRT's does NOT — ucrtbase's detach flushes streams but never runs the app's onexit table, because in a real MSVC program that table is drained by `exit()` itself, in the static CRT startup code. So after the co-state-group flip, `ExitProcess` would have left `_crt_atexit`-registered handlers REGISTERED AND NEVER CALLED: a silent, no-diagnostic behavioural regression introduced by the migration itself. Repointing the spine at ucrtbase `exit` is the fix, and it must land in the SAME commit as stdlib.json's `atexit` -> `_crt_atexit` rename — the two are one change. `exit` is dual-exported (MEASURED at TF-C111, `objdump -p`: ucrtbase YES / msvcrt YES), so this is not a UCRT-only dependency.

THREE THINGS THIS BUYS BEYOND FIXING THE REGRESSION. (1) C CONFORMANCE: C 5.1.2.2.3 makes returning from main equivalent to calling `exit` with that value, which requires the atexit handlers to run and the streams to be flushed IN THAT ORDER — `exit` does exactly that; a raw process-kill primitive cannot. (2) UNIFORMITY: the 'terminate through a stdio-flushing libc-level primitive on every hosted format' mandate is now realized the SAME way everywhere — elf->libc `exit`, macho->libSystem `exit` (symbol `_exit`), pe->CRT `exit` — instead of pe being the one format that reached for an OS primitive and relied on a DLL-detach side effect to look equivalent. (3) It DE-couples the spine from an OS export in favour of the C library the program is already bound to. Stdout delivery is unchanged and still witnessed by the `puts("hello")`-then-return corpus (examples/c/shipped_include_puts, hello_puts), which prints 'hello\r\n' on Windows under captured-pipe stdout — the \r\n is CRT text-mode CRLF translation, confirming the bytes flow through the CRT FILE layer; examples/c/shipped_atexit is the handler-ordering witness (byte-exact stdout, exit 42) and goes RED on the Windows ctest leg if this row and stdlib.json's macro disagree.

NOTE — SUPERSEDED BY UCRT-P4 (landed `64ee3a16`), AND THE SENTENCE IT REPLACES IS KEPT HERE RATHER THAN DELETED, for the same reason the ExitProcess argument above is kept: the reasoning is load-bearing and the way it went wrong is the lesson. It read: 'this does NOT make the pe spine msvcrt-free. `processArgs.crtLibraryPath` below is still msvcrt.dll, because `__getmainargs`/`__wgetmainargs` are msvcrt-ONLY exports (MEASURED: ucrtbase exports neither) and their UCRT replacement is a different mechanism (`_configure_narrow_argv` + `__p___argc`/`__p___argv`). That is P4/P5 scope.' ★ EVERY MEASUREMENT IN THAT SENTENCE IS STILL TRUE; ONLY ITS CONCLUSION EXPIRED, because P4 went and did the thing the last clause deferred. WHAT ACTUALLY CHANGED: `processArgs` was NOT repointed — its MECHANISM CHANGED, to `crt-argv-accessors` over precisely the UCRT replacement that sentence names, and the key `crtLibraryPath` — the literal this note pointed AT — no longer exists in this file or in any other config file. The image is now named by ROLE (`role: cLibrary`) and resolved against the `runtimeLibraries` ROLE -> IMAGE table above, so there is no per-block library literal left to go stale. Read `$processArgsComment` below for the mechanism and `$runtimeLibrariesComment` above for the table. ⇒ THE pe SPINE IS msvcrt-FREE. ★★ AND THE CRITERION THAT ENTITLES ANYONE TO SAY SO IS FOUR CLAUSES, NOT ONE — which is the durable half of this correction: (i) no shipped descriptor names `msvcrt.dll` (MEASURED 2026-08-11 over all 49 descriptors counted RECURSIVELY: 16 `ucrtbase.dll` + 2 `kernel32.dll` = 18 pe entries, ZERO msvcrt, and 0 per-symbol library overrides); (ii) the startup argv path names no msvcrt export; (iii) no language-level per-format extern default binds msvcrt (`externLibraryByFormat` was DELETED from `c.lang.json`, not flipped); (iv) the abort-behaviour surface is a REAL binding, not a no-op macro (`stdlib.json`'s `_set_abort_behavior`). ⚠ The SINGLE-clause criterion in force when this note was first written — clause (i) alone — would have certified the whole arc COMPLETE while three of those four surfaces were still live, one of which P3 itself created. See D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION. The mechanism stays config-driven per format, with NO format identity branch in the shared trampoline.
$runtimeLibrariesComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION): the ROLE -> IMAGE table, and the SINGLE OWNER of 'which image plays which runtime role' for this format. Every spine block below names a ROLE (processExit.role / processArgs.role / sehPersonality.role / librarySynthesis.role) and the loader resolves it here; the resolved path each block carries in memory is a DERIVED copy, and ObjectFormatData::validate() re-checks the pair, so the two can never drift. WHY A TABLE AND NOT ONE `crt` STRING: a single string models an ACCIDENT of one DLL configuration and is already wrong in two configurations this repo ships. (1) MEASURED 2026-08-10 (`nm -D`): the ELF unwinder personality lives in libgcc_s.so.1 and libc.so.6 exports NO `_Unwind_*` at all -- do NOT be fooled by `personality@@GLIBC_2.2.5` in libc, that is the personality(2) SYSCALL wrapper -- so on ELF one image demonstrably cannot serve both cLibrary and unwindPersonality. (2) Microsoft names the C library and the VC runtime SEPARATELY in BOTH configurations (/MD -> ucrt.lib + vcruntime.lib; /MT -> libucrt.lib + libvcruntime.lib) and DSS already ships static linking for all formats (#47), so the split configuration is live in-tree. (3) ucrtbase ALSO exporting `__C_specific_handler` (MEASURED ord 30; msvcrt 106, ntdll 2332, vcruntime140 8) is a CONVENIENCE of the pe DLL config, not Microsoft's model. * cLibrary and unwindPersonality pointing at the SAME image here is FINE: the table PERMITS sameness without ASSERTING it, which is the whole difference from a single string and is what stops the value having to be re-cut every time a new configuration arrives (D-TEST-PE64-CONFOUND-PIN-WEAKENED-BY-ITS-OWN-SUBJECT). * systemPrimitives is kernel32.dll and is DELIBERATELY not the C library: the Win32 synthesis vehicle emits over OS primitives (CRITICAL_SECTION / CONDITION_VARIABLE / Fls*), whereas the Mach-O sibling's pthread vehicle rides libSystem, which IS its C library -- that asymmetry is unexpressible in a single string. * THE MECHANICAL EXIT CRITERION for the pe CRT migration is stated against THIS block: no pe format file's runtimeLibraries table may name msvcrt.dll, checked across all four pe flavours (exec, dll, staticlib, obj). It is strictly stronger than a single-CRT-string criterion because it also catches a future edit repointing ONE role at the wrong image. RED-ON-DISABLE (both directions, MEASURED by doing it): DELETE a row and every block naming that role refuses the format AT LOAD, naming this file; ADD a row nothing names and validate() refuses it as inert config. * MINIMUM-WINDOWS FLOOR (D-LK-PE-EXEC-HARD-DEPENDS-ON-UCRTBASE-AFTER-PROCESSEXIT-REPOINT): ucrtbase.dll ships in-box from Windows 10 (build 10240) onward and via the redistributable KB2999226 on 7 SP1 / 8 / 8.1; msvcrt.dll shipped in-box much earlier. So repointing the spine at ucrtbase raises this format's effective floor to Windows 10 in-box, or 7 SP1 + the UCRT redistributable. kernel32.dll (systemPrimitives) has no such floor.
$processArgsComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION, replacing c111's msvcrt arm): the Windows program-entry argc/argv mechanism. Unlike ELF/Mach-O (where the OS entry receives the argument vector on the stack / in registers), the PE OS entry gets NOTHING -- the C runtime must ASK for the arguments. c111 asked msvcrt via `__getmainargs`/`__wgetmainargs` out-parameters; those are msvcrt-ONLY exports (MEASURED 2026-08-10, `objdump -p`: msvcrt ord 138 / 167, ucrtbase exports NEITHER), so they cannot survive the UCRT migration and the mechanism CHANGES rather than being repointed. UCRT publishes a different shape: one populate call `_configure_narrow_argv(int mode)` (ord 190) / `_configure_wide_argv` (191), then three ADDRESS-returning accessors `__p___argc` -> int* (81), `__p___argv` -> char*** (82), `__p___wargv` -> wchar_t*** (83), each needing EXACTLY ONE dereference (ucrt/stdlib.h:1144-1145, macros :1153-1154). * PROBE-0, MEASURED 2026-08-10 AND THE REASON THIS WORKS AT ALL: the accessor triple returns the REAL command line in a STARTUP-LESS DSS pe64 binary, byte-identical to the `__getmainargs` control, at debug AND release. NO `_initterm` prologue and NO `__acrt_initialize` are needed. `_configure_narrow_argv` IS load-bearing -- without it `*__p___argc()==0` and `*__p___argv()==NULL`. * `mechanism: crt-argv-accessors` drives the MIR-tier entry-shape pass (src/mir/merge/synth_pe_startup.cpp), which synthesizes a pre-main init `int _dss_pe_start()` that makes the populate call, dereferences the two accessors, GATES on argv, then forwards (argc, argv) to the user entry -- and retargets the program entry to that synth function. The entry-trampoline emits NO argument materialization for this mechanism; the synth init owns it. Contrast ELF/AArch64's stack-vector arm, which the trampoline materializes directly. * WIDE vs NARROW is chosen by the RESOLVED ENTRY'S SIGNATURE, never a format flag -- unchanged from c111 in principle, sharpened in mechanism: the LANGUAGE entry row that MATCHES the entry carries the verb (this file declares only which verbs it can realize), so `wmain(int, wchar_t**)` matches the ptr-ptr-u16 row -> `argc-wargv` -> the wide names, and `main(int, char**)` matches ptr-ptr-char -> `argc-argv` -> the narrow ones. argc is SHARED between the narrow and wide worlds (MEASURED, PROBE-0), so ONE accessor serves both and there is no wide argc name. * `argvMode` is `_crt_argv_mode`, whose enum lives in .../VC/Tools/MSVC/<ver>/include/vcruntime_startup.h:19-24 -- the MSVC TOOLSET header, NOT the Windows SDK (a grep of the SDK include tree for the enumerator names returns zero hits). MEASURED with a literal `*.c` argument and two .c files present: mode 0 -> argc 0 / argv NULL; mode 1 -> argc 4 with argv[3]=="*.c" LITERAL; mode 2 -> argc 5, glob EXPANDED. c111 passed `_dowildcard = 0` (unexpanded), so mode 1 is the BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING choice. The loader constrains the value to 0..2: mode 7 does not return an error at all, the process dies at 0xC0000409 printing nothing, so load time is the only tier that can refuse it. * `argvUnavailableExitStatus` exists because THE RETURN VALUE CANNOT BE TRUSTED (MEASURED): all three valid modes return errno_t 0, and mode 0 returns 0 WHILE YIELDING argv == NULL. So the emitted gate tests `*__p___argv() != NULL`, never the errno_t -- which would be a guard that asserts nothing. On failure the init RETURNS 127 instead of calling the user entry, so the status flows out through this format's already-wired processExit path (no second exit import, no Unreachable in a reachable position) and the program terminates with a distinctive code rather than running main on a NULL argv. * The import library is named by ROLE (cLibrary), not spelled here -- see $runtimeLibrariesComment.
$entryVerbsComment: UCRT-P4 (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE): the program-entry materialization VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE -- what it is able to hand a program entry before calling it. * THE ACCEPTED ENTRY SET IS AN INTERSECTION, AND THIS FILE OWNS ONLY HALF OF IT. This key used to be `entryShapes` -- full { returns, params, materialization } rows -- which made the accepted SIGNATURES a format fact. They are not one: `int wmain(int, wchar_t**)` is a C spelling, and a linker format has no opinion on how a source language spells an entry, only on what it can hand one. So the signatures moved to their single owner, the language file's `entryFunctions` mapping (src/dss-config/sources/c.lang.json), which declares each name->signature->verb; this key declares the VERBS THIS FORMAT CAN REALIZE. A defined function is a program-entry candidate iff its name matches a declared language row, its signature matches that row, and that row's verb appears HERE. C23 3.4.1 requires an implementation to DOCUMENT its implementation-defined choices, so the documentation artifact is the PAIR of comments -- this one and $entryFunctionsComment -- each naming the other. Reading either alone tells you less than the truth. * THIS IS THE ONLY SHIPPED FORMAT THAT REALIZES `argc-wargv`, and that single fact is what makes `wmain` a program entry on Windows and nowhere else. The verb is realizable here because the UCRT publishes a wide vector: processArgs above declares `crt-argv-accessors` with _configure_wide_argv + __p___wargv, so the MIR-tier init can actually produce one. WIDE vs NARROW is still chosen by the RESOLVED ENTRY'S SIGNATURE and never by a format flag -- the language row that matches the entry carries the verb, so `wmain(int, unsigned short**)` matches the ptr-ptr-u16 row -> argc-wargv -> the wide export names, and `main(int, char**)` matches ptr-ptr-char -> argc-argv -> the narrow ones. * CONSEQUENCE WORTH STATING PLAINLY: because BOTH verbs are realized here, a program defining BOTH `main` and `wmain` has TWO surviving candidates on this format and is REFUSED as ambiguous (K_ProgramEntryAmbiguous). The identical source BUILDS on ELF and Mach-O and takes `main`, because `wmain`'s verb does not survive the intersection there. That divergence is CORRECT and deliberate: it is MSVC's own ambiguity, and picking one silently is the defect. * WHY THERE IS NO envp VERB: same as the ELF files -- it needs its own emitter and its own RUN witness (D-RUNTIME-MAIN-ENVP-ENTRY-SHAPE), and the pairing rule above already refuses a `crt-argv-accessors` mechanism whose verbs would leave the declared CRT export names dead. * `none` is the verb `int main(void)` needs; declaring it is an ANSWER, not an omission. * RED-ON-DISABLE: drop "argc-argv" from this list and every example whose entry is `main(int, char**)` becomes unresolvable on this format -- the language's argc-argv row no longer survives the intersection, so the program has no entry candidate at all and the build is REFUSED naming this key. Empty the list entirely and the format is refused AT LOAD (exec-flavored <-> non-empty entryVerbs is pinned in both directions), because the engine reads this emptiness as "this format starts no program".
$sehPersonalityComment: UCRT-P4 (D-FFI-PE-CRT-UCRT-MIGRATION + D-WIN64-SEH-FUNCLETS): the routine an emitted UNWIND_INFO names as its EHANDLER, and the ROLE that owns the image it is imported from. WHAT THIS REPLACES: src/mir/merge/synth_seh_funclets.cpp hardcoded BOTH `pers.mangledName = "__C_specific_handler"` AND `pers.libraryPath = "msvcrt.dll"` -- two platform literals in shared MIR substrate, on a pass that runs for EVERY format, which no format could override and no test could see. SEH (`__try`/`__except`) is NOT C23; it is a Microsoft extension, and that is PRECISELY why its personality must be a per-format CONFIG DECLARATION rather than a literal inside src/mir. The role is unwindPersonality rather than cLibrary even though both resolve to ucrtbase.dll here: sameness is a fact about this DLL configuration, not about the model (Microsoft names the C library and the VC runtime separately in both /MD and /MT). MEASURED 2026-08-10 that the move is link-safe either way: `__C_specific_handler` is exported by ucrtbase (ord 30), msvcrt (106), ntdll (2332) AND vcruntime140 (8). A format declaring NO sehPersonality now fails LOUD the moment a guarded region resolves -- which is what an ELF or Mach-O build carrying `__try` should get instead of an msvcrt import in an ELF image.
$entryCallingConventionComment: MS x64 calling convention — status (user fn return value in rax) is moved into argGprs[0] = rcx before the indirect ExitProcess call. Read via `target.callingConventionByName("ms_x64")` at trampoline-build time.
$supportedDataSectionsComment: D-LK2-RODATA (`.rdata`) + D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER (writable `.data` + uninitialized `.bss`) + D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL (thread-local `tdata`/`tbss`, TLS C3): the PE-Exec walker emits `.rdata` (read-only), `.data` (mutable initialized globals, MEM_WRITE), `.bss` (zero-init globals, CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA — SizeOfRawData=0), and `.tls` (the thread-local TEMPLATE) from `AssembledModule.dataItems` per the item's `section`. BOTH `tdata` (initialized `thread_local int g = 7;`) AND `tbss` (zero-init `thread_local int g;`) are advertised: PE folds a `tbss` item into the ONE `.tls` section's IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64 `SizeOfZeroFill` tail (no separate `.tbss` section) — but a bare `thread_local int g;` IS a `tbss` item, so omitting `tbss` from this set would make the linker's pre-walker gate reject a valid program (M-1). The linker's gate consults this set per-item. Cross-format agnosticism: this is the SAME field ELF/Mach-O exec formats declare; zero linker source changes.
$relroExecComment: D-LK-RELRO-CONST-DATA-RELOCATABLE (c145): `relro` (a CONST global carrying LOAD-TIME relocations — a const function-pointer table, e.g. sqlite os_win.c aSyscall[]) is advertised so the linker's pre-walker gate admits it. In the PE32+ image the walker FOLDS a relro item into the read-only `.rdata` section (PE base-relocates `.rdata` — the loader applies the IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 base-relocation into the slot BEFORE the page is sealed read-only, exactly as it already does for F5 symbol-address global pointers), so NO separate relro section row is declared here — relro rides `.rdata` and its abs64 fixups join the existing `.reloc` DIR64 table.
$tlsAccessComment: TLS C3 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): how code reaches a thread-local object's per-thread copy on Windows x86_64 — the SAME x86 primitive ELF uses, config-only differences (model + segment + displacement). pe-indexed = the Windows TEB-slot-array model: `mov rax, gs:[0x58]` (segmentPrefixByte 101 = 0x65 gs-override, baseDisplacement 88 = 0x58 = TEB.ThreadLocalStoragePointer) reads the per-thread array of module TLS-block pointers; `mov ecx, [__dss_tls_index]` (the writer-minted module TLS index singleton — tlsIndexSlotName; a 32-BIT read, the loader fills the slot with this module's index) selects THIS module's block; `mov rax, [rax + rcx*8]` loads the block base; `lea rax, [rax + secrel32(sym)]` adds the variable's POSITIVE section-relative offset within the `.tls` template (the tls-tpoff32 reloc, kind 4 = IMAGE_REL_AMD64_SECREL here). The Windows loader processes IMAGE_DIRECTORY_ENTRY_TLS for the main thread BEFORE the entry point AND allocates+copies a fresh block per CreateThread — so per-thread storage is real. The SAME `tlsbase` opcode row serves ELF (fs) and PE (gs); a format WITHOUT this block fails loud K_FormatLacksThreadLocalSupport on the first thread-local access.
$librarySynthesisComment: D-CSUBSET-C11-THREADS-MACHO (opened for the pe/macho vehicle split): the Windows CRT exports NO C11 <threads.h> symbols, so each thrd_*/mtx_*/cnd_*/tss_* function is a COMPILER-SYNTHESIZED shim (src/mir/merge/synth_threads_shim.cpp, the `win32` vehicle) emitted over kernel32 CRITICAL_SECTION / CONDITION_VARIABLE / Fls* primitives. libraryPath is the DLL the on-demand kernel32 helpers import from — the value that DISSOLVES the pass's former hardcoded "kernel32.dll" literal (now config-sourced for BOTH vehicles). Keyed by the FORMAT; the synth pass dispatches on this declared verb, never on a format identity.
$stackReserveControlComment: D-SQLITE-PE64-FULL-TIER-STACK-DEPTH: this format CAN carry a per-PROGRAM stack reserve, so it declares the capability; PRESENCE is what the linker gate reads (`ObjectFormatSchema::stackReserveControl()`), never a format identity. A program's required stack is a property of ITS deepest call chain, not of the format, so the `optionalHeader.sizeOfStackReserve` value below is only the DEFAULT (1 MiB — the MSVC/Windows convention); a project manifest `stackReserve` / CLI `--stack-reserve` OVERRIDES it. MEASURED motivation: the sqlite full-source testfixture dies at `e_fkey-63.1.1` (1000 levels of nested trigger recursion) at 1 MiB — and so does a GCC-built native testfixture at a MATCHED 1 MiB reserve (bisected minimum 1.75 MB gcc / 3.38 MB DSS), so this is a genuine per-program need, not a codegen workaround (the ~1.93x frame-size gap is separately anchored, D-CODEGEN-FRAME-SIZE-VS-NATIVE-2X). vehicle `pe-optional-header` = IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64.SizeOfStackReserve at optional-header offset +72, written by `src/link/format/pe.cpp`'s image arm. NOTE the deliberate asymmetry with the SIBLING schemas: `pe64-x86_64-windows-dll.format.json` has the SAME header field but declares NO capability (the loader IGNORES a DLL's SizeOfStackReserve — the .exe's value governs the main thread, and other threads take the .exe default or an explicit CreateThread size), and the `.obj` schema has no optional header at all. That is exactly why the capability is per-FORMAT config: an `if (kind == pe)` engine branch would happily write a field nothing reads. ELF declares nothing because no ELF image field carries a stack SIZE (PT_GNU_STACK encodes EXECUTABILITY; the size is a runtime/`ulimit -s` property) — a request on an ELF target fails LOUD rather than being dropped. minimumBytes = 65536 (the Windows 64 KiB allocation granularity — the smallest reserve the VM manager can actually distinguish); maximumBytes = 4294967296 (4 GiB — a reserve is VIRTUAL address space so a generous cap is right; the bound exists to fail a fat-fingered value loud at link instead of shipping an image the loader refuses); granularityBytes = 4096 (page). A request outside the range or off the granularity is REFUSED, never clamped or rounded.
$artifactProfilesComment: Profiles this format SERVES (plan 06 AP3) — a runnable console executable ⇒ cli (the format-side twin of the language's artifactProfiles[]; driver fails loud D_ArtifactProfileFormatMismatch on a profile not in this set). A `gui` profile (IMAGE_SUBSYSTEM_WINDOWS_GUI) would be added when gui codegen lands — same format, profile-selected subsystem/entry, zero gate-code change.

pe.$comment: IMAGE_FILE_HEADER identity. machine = IMAGE_FILE_MACHINE_AMD64 (0x8664). characteristics = IMAGE_FILE_EXECUTABLE_IMAGE (0x0002) | IMAGE_FILE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE (0x0020) = 0x0022. type = exec.

optionalHeader.$comment: IMAGE_OPTIONAL_HEADER64 (PE/COFF spec §3.4). magic = PE32+ (0x20B). imageBase = 0x140000000 (Windows x86_64 .exe default per MSVC). sectionAlignment = 0x1000 (4 KB virtual). fileAlignment = 0x200 (512 raw). subsystem = WINDOWS_CUI (3). dllCharacteristics = HIGH_ENTROPY_VA (0x0020) | DYNAMIC_BASE (0x0040) | NX_COMPAT (0x0100) | TERMINAL_SERVER_AWARE (0x8000) = 0x8160 (ASLR + DEP enabled). Stack/heap reserve = 1 MiB; commit = 4 KiB (MSVC defaults). OS/Subsystem versions = 6.0 (Windows Vista — minimum modern target).

sections.$comment: Executable code section. virtualAddress = 0x1000 — first page after the headers (which occupy [0, sectionAlignment) inside the ImageBase mapping). Characteristics = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_CODE (0x00000020) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_EXECUTE (0x20000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_ALIGN_16BYTES (0x00500000) = 0x60500020. Same value as the .obj schema's `.text` Characteristics (alignment + read/execute) — the PE32+ image just adds the RVA via the substrate `virtualAddress` field.
sections.name: .text

sections.$comment: Read-only data section (D-LK2-RODATA closure). Emitted by the PE walker between .text and .idata when `AssembledModule.dataItems` carries any item with `section==Rodata`. virtualAddress=0 here is a placeholder — the walker computes the actual RVA at emit time as (textVirtualAddress + textVirtualSize) since sections must be contiguous in VA space. Characteristics = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x00000040) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) = 0x40000040 — initialized data, read-only (no write, no execute). The walker reads the section name + characteristics from this row; the VA is computed dynamically from layout.
sections.name: .rdata

sections.$comment: Writable initialized data (mutable globals) — D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER. Emitted by the PE walker after .rdata when AssembledModule.dataItems carries an item with section==Data. virtualAddress=0 is a placeholder — the walker computes the RVA at emit time (contiguous after .rdata). Characteristics (the substrate `type` field) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x00000040) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000040 = 3221225536 — initialized data, READ + WRITE (the MEM_WRITE bit is what makes a runtime store legal; a .rdata store faults). The walker reads name + characteristics from this row.
sections.name: .data

sections.$comment: Uninitialized data (tentative globals `int g;`) — D-LK4-DATA-PRODUCER. Emitted by the PE walker after .data. SizeOfRawData=0 / PointerToRawData=0 (NO file footprint — the loader zero-fills VirtualSize bytes); contributes to SizeOfUninitializedData. virtualAddress=0 — walker-computed. Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_UNINITIALIZED_DATA (0x00000080) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000080 = 3221225600 — uninitialized data, READ + WRITE.
sections.name: .bss

sections.$comment: Thread-local TEMPLATE section (`thread_local` — D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL, TLS C3). ONE `.tls` section carries the INITIALIZED per-thread template bytes (the `tdata` items); a zero-init `thread_local int g;` (`tbss`) item contributes NO file bytes — it is folded into the IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64 `SizeOfZeroFill` tail, so there is NO separate `.tbss` section (this `kind: tdata` row is looked up by the walker for the SECTION NAME + Characteristics; the tbss span rides the directory). The walker also lays the 40-byte IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64 + the 4-byte `_tls_index` slot at the tail of THIS section (both past the template span [StartAddressOfRawData, EndAddressOfRawData) so they are never per-thread-copied); a writable section is a valid home for the loader-read directory AND the loader-written index. Characteristics (`type`) = IMAGE_SCN_CNT_INITIALIZED_DATA (0x40) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_READ (0x40000000) | IMAGE_SCN_MEM_WRITE (0x80000000) = 0xC0000040 = 3221225536 — the loader applies base relocations into the template + directory VA fields (requires MEM_WRITE) and each thread's copy is writable. virtualAddress=0 — walker-computed (contiguous after the prior data section).
sections.name: .tls

relocations.$comment: PE32+ image-side relocations: same kinds as the .obj schema. cycle-2 walker applies intra-module relocs in-place via the LK6 cycle 1 structured-formula triple (closes D-LK1-3-equivalent for PE). REL32 is PC-relative 32-bit; ADDR64/ADDR32 are absolute. The image is ASLR-aware (dllCharacteristics carries DYNAMIC_BASE), so the walker DOES emit a `.reloc` base-relocation section carrying an IMAGE_REL_BASED_DIR64 entry per 8-byte absolute fixup: the cross-CU thunk slots + F5 symbol-address global pointers + (TLS C3) the 3 IMAGE_TLS_DIRECTORY64 VA fields.
relocations.name: IMAGE_REL_AMD64_REL32

relocations.$comment: TLS C3 (D-CSUBSET-THREAD-LOCAL): the thread-local SECTION-RELATIVE fixup — the disp32 of `lea rax, [rax + secrel32(sym)]`, the FINAL instruction of the pe-indexed access sequence. kind=4 is the SHARED target-schema `tls-tpoff32` row (Linear, width 4, absolute, tls:true) — x86_64 serves BOTH ELF and PE from ONE `[reg, symbol]` lea variant, so the ELF↔PE split lives HERE at the FORMAT level (this row) not on the target (mirrors elf64's kind-4 `R_X86_64_TPOFF32`). The walker patches the 4 bytes from its POSITIVE templateOffset-valued symbolVa entry (the variable's byte offset within the `.tls` template — NOT the ELF NEGATIVE tpoff), so `blockBase + templateOffset` = the per-thread address; the image carries NO runtime reloc for this disp32 (it is an ASLR-invariant relative offset, a link-time constant). nativeId = IMAGE_REL_AMD64_SECREL (11) — meaningful only for a future .obj emission of this kind; the row's existence satisfies the linker's pre-walker cross-reference unifier + the walker's in-arm tls-kind check (the CRIT-1 XOR backstop).
relocations.name: IMAGE_REL_AMD64_SECREL
